correctness.rationale: Proper completed part palettes are disjoint. A part with at least two colours in the completion can never have a forced vertex, since its neighbours use at most Q−2 colours. The first force witnesses Q−1 outside colours and completes that palette with the remaining colour, so any successful non-total seed has a surjective completion, with all parts containing blanks monochromatic. Two wholly empty monochromatic parts would leave at least two colours absent and prevent even the first step. Conversely, when exactly one such part is empty it is forceable first, and once every part is represented every remaining blank sees exactly the other Q−1 colours. The forced colour is necessary in any extension, giving uniqueness and ensuring the enumerator does not double count across completions. Partition into unlabelled nonempty colour classes and injectively label them for the falling-factorial Stirling count. For each surjective completion factor the allowed seed restrictions by part, with at most one constant-term omission among the monochromatic factors, and subtract the total term already counted by P_G(Q). Multiplying powers by the independent assignment probabilities gives the probability transform including its polynomial endpoint. In the balanced case, the number j of nonsingle-colour parts among non-total successes must satisfy j≤r−1 and j≤d≤j(t−1). Their least seed size is jt+r−j−1; since it increases with j the first admissible j is k, attained by the one omitted monochromatic part and singleton seeds in the others. Summing colour-class partitions over the bounded positive compositions of d gives the claimed leading coefficient; above the capacity cutoff only total seeds remain, also for Q>N. Independently checked the K_(2,2,2) coefficients for Q=4,5,6 and the total-only Q=7 case by counting partial assignments with exactly one proper full extension (replay python3 /tmp/opencode/nov02-independent-checks.py 4). For this graph class unique completion implies forcing: one can otherwise recolour a blank vertex in a multicolour part or with an unused palette colour, or interchange the colours of two wholly unseeded monochromatic parts. The local process was also independently simulated on the three displayed examples. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; finite tests corroborate rather than establish the theorem.

evidence: The Q≥r+2 record minimizes r−1+sum_(i∈H)(n_i−1) over proper sets H with |H|≤Q−r≤sum_(i∈H)(n_i−1), with the default N if none is feasible.
For equal t this minimum is r−1+(t−1)⌈(Q−r)/(t−1)⌉ when feasible, and feasibility ends at (r−1)(t−1). The prior Q=r+1 minimum gives the first step as well.
Farr gives a general colour-count necessity and a two-colour bipartite theorem, neither providing the claimed surplus census on its own.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier minimum is already exact on heterogeneous parts. Equal capacities turn its subset optimization directly into the stated staircase, including the terminal cutoff.

evidence: In an equal-size surjective profile with j multicolour parts, the smallest exponent of prior B_t is jt+r−j−1; its coefficient is (r−j)t^(r−j−1) (choose the single omission and the least-degree term t·x from every other monochromatic part). Only j=k can contribute at the global least exponent.

Sum the prior Stirling product over the k chosen parts and over t_i−1≥1 summing to d, giving exactly binom(r,k)(r−k)t^(r−k−1)Q! times the stated coefficient of the kth power; Q=r+1 also follows by specializing the prior split-part minimum count.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The explicit leading-coefficient expression is a straightforward extraction from the prior all-coefficient polynomial and minimum, even if it was not printed in that notation. No nontrivial remainder survives the union of the two earlier parameter ranges.

evidence: For Q≥r+2 set λ=Q, t_i=s_i, x=z. Prior B_t=H_s; it omits profiles with M empty, whose H_s−z^N is zero. It uses exactly the same iterative rule, named colours, and count of total seeds.

For Q=r+1 the only surjective profiles have one split j, with S(n_j,2)=(2^{n_j}−2)/2, and nonsurjective completions use one colour on every part, exactly (r+1)! of them. The two resulting terms are precisely the prior H_G.

The general Farr implication forcing⇒unique extension can be reversed for complete multipartite graphs by the recolouring and empty-part symmetry argument described in correctness, so unique extensions are a scientifically relevant alias but not needed to establish the overlap.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: After identifying labels, omissions and coefficients the earlier two enumerators are algebraically identical in complementary ranges; the overlap does not rest on use of the word forcing.

residual_risks: The comparison does not establish worldwide historical priority or rule out older defining-set and unique-extension literature. The exact prior multipartite results suffice regardless.
